title: organization delete keeps engine-owned rows that a user still sees: inbox messages stay in the bell for up to 90 days
body:
domain:server#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaAUev5V62cLHhQwBi

Filing category: ③ product question for the owning seat, a family question (escalated by the CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER review of PR #32490 for #32444, comment 6811790848, nit N1; read from the code, not run).
Refs #32444

## Business reason

When an organization is deleted, its members expect what the organization sent them to go with it. Some rows the platform writes are kept on purpose, such as audit and history. But a kept row that is still shown to a person reads as live content from an organization that no longer exists.

## What happens

1. `ObjectQL.outlivesOrganization` (`packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts`) keeps every row of an object whose `managedBy` is `append-only` or `engine-owned`. It neither counts nor deletes them on organization delete (seat decisions 6305179819 and 6307135388).
2. After PR #32490, `sys_inbox_message` is `engine-owned`, so its rows join that set. The PR's changeset declares it.
3. `listInbox` reads with `where: { user_id }` under `INBOX_SYSTEM_CONTEXT`, with no organization term. So a kept inbox row from the deleted organization is still served in the recipient's bell until the 90-day `ttl` reaper removes it.
4. The same rule applies to every `engine-owned` object (approval state, automation runs, deliveries, mirrored mail, record shares, import jobs, settings values). Whether any other of them is still shown to an end user after the delete was not checked.

## Expected

The owning seat decides, for the `engine-owned` family, whether a kept row may stay visible to end users after its organization is deleted. Possible shapes: the rule stays and is documented; the readers that show such rows to users filter out rows of a deleted organization; or particular objects (the inbox first) are cleaned on organization delete although they are engine-owned.

Re-check (premise): read `outlivesOrganization` and `listInbox` (`packages/services/service-messaging/src`) on main after #32490 lands.
Reader who acts: the seat that owns `packages/objectql` organization-delete cascade planning, with the messaging owner for the inbox.
